newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were steady to $0.50 per cwt lower early Wednesday, pressured by an increase in hog movement as temperatures cool and humidity comes down, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $58.00 to $59.00 in the country and $59.00 to $60.50 at plants.
"I wouldn't say it was a big run of hogs we're seeing, but we got all we needed," a central Iowa packer buyer said.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $59.00 to $60.00 in the country and $60.00 to $60.50 at plants.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower at $59.00 to $60.00 in the country and $60.00 to $61.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold steady at $57.50 to $58.00 in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants, the dealers said.
Extreme heat and humidity Monday in much of the Corn Belt and the eastern belt on Tuesday reportedly limited hog marketings. Heat was still a factor from central Indiana into Ohio, they said.
The heat and humidity can increase stress and death loss and if extended can reduce rates of gain, the dealers said.
However, as weather conditions improved, marketings slowly expanded, they said.
